Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The Umpires and the players take the field to start the Run chase. Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique are the opening batters for Pakistan. Kagiso Rabada has the new ball in hand and is ready to start the second innings. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With 240 runs as the target, Pakistan have a good chance to start the ODI series on a high. Will they chase it down easily, or will the South African bowlers have a magic trick up their sleeve to stop them from getting to the target? Let's find out in the Run Chase!

Heinrich Klaasen is up for a chat and says that the score on the board could be enough if they bowl and field well. Adds that it felt like a normal Paarl wicket and you need to do the hard work on it and a couple of wickets when the off-spinner came on was a big blow. Reckons that bowling the right lines and lengths could make it challenging for the batters.

Captain Aiden Markram and Heinrich Klaasen then mounted a recovery, sharing a vital 73-run partnership. Markram, however, fell to a mistimed pull shot off Saim Ayub. Klaasen continued to anchor the innings and received support from Marco Jansen, with the pair adding another 50 runs. Jansen was eventually removed by Abrar Ahmed, leaving Klaasen to fight a lone battle. Despite Klaasen’s determined knock, he fell just 14 runs short of a century, with wickets tumbling at the other end. Kagiso Rabada and Ottneil Baartman added 25 runs for the last wicket, pushing South Africa to a respectable 239/9.

South Africa started strongly, with Tony de Zorzi and Ryan Rickelton putting together a 70-run opening stand inside the first 10 overs. However, Agha Salman turned the game on its head with a sensational spell, dismissing both openers as well as Rassie van der Dussen and Tristan Stubbs. His four wickets in quick succession left the South African innings in disarray.

With that, we come to the end of the First Innings of the match and after being 94/4 inside the first 15 overs, South Africa manages to score 239/9 after batting the whole 50 overs, thanks to Heinrich Klaasen with his 86. Pakistan will be happy walking back into the hut as they will have to come out and chase 240 runs in their allotted quota of 50 overs. Pakistan put on an impressive bowling display to restrict South Africa to 239/9 in their 50 overs after the hosts opted to bat first. Agha Salman was the standout performer, taking four crucial wickets and dismantling the Proteas' batting order during his first spell.

A RUN OUT TO END THE FIRST INNINGS! Haris Rauf digs in a shortish ball over leg and right at the body of the batter. Kagiso Rabada hangs back and looks to take it on but skews it high up and just over the mid-wicket region. The ball falls in between three fielders but the throw from Irfan Khan is a good one at the keeper's end. Mohammad Rizwan whips off the bails and replays show that it was poor running from Rabada who is just short of his crease and it will only be a single. South Africa finish with 239/9 on the board!

With the Champions Trophy approaching, South Africa has assembled a formidable squad led by the in-form Temba Bavuma, strengthened by the inclusion of power hitters David Miller and Heinrich Klaasen. Fresh off his impressive performance in the T20I series, Ryan Rickelton is expected to open alongside Temba Bavuma, with Tony Zorzi providing an alternative option at the top. The Proteas boast a robust middle order featuring the experienced Rassie van der Dussen, alongside the dynamic Tristan Stubbs, David Miller, and Heinrich Klaasen. Meanwhile, Aiden Markram will be keen to rediscover his form, having struggled to make significant contributions in recent outings. However, South Africa's pace bowling department faces significant challenges, with several key players sidelined due to injuries - Anrich Nortje, Gerald Coetzee, Wiaan Mulder, and Lungi Ngidi all unavailable. This has opened the door for 18-year-old sensation Kwena Maphaka, who recently topped the wicket-taking charts at the U-19 World Cup. The young pacer will share new-ball responsibilities with seasoned campaigner Kagiso Rabada, while Ottneil Baartman provides an additional fast-bowling option as the Proteas look to manage their depleted pace resources. Pace-bowling all-rounders like Andile Phehlukwayo and Marco Jansen and spinners Keshav Maharaj along side Tabraiz Shamsi, round up South Africa’s squad. Following their underwhelming performance in the T20I series, Pakistan seeks redemption as they transition to the ODI format. Under the leadership of Mohammad Rizwan, the team appears formidable on paper, despite their recent struggles. Pakistan's batting lineup features an intriguing blend of youth and experience at the top, with emerging talent Saim Ayub partnering the technically sound Abdullah Shafique as openers. The middle order carries significant firepower with the proven duo of Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan, complemented by the inclusion of Usman Khan. Salman Ali Agha adds versatility to the squad, offering both batting depth and valuable spin-bowling options. Pakistan's trademark strength lies in their pace attack, where the formidable trio of Naseem Shah, Haris Rauf, and Shaheen Shah Afridi stands ready to challenge the South African batters. This potent fast-bowling combination will be eager to make their mark in the ODI series and especially on pace-friendly South African pitches. Spin duties will be heavily rely on the likes of Abrar Ahmed while they have Sufiyan Muqeem as another emerging talent in this facet. The most recent ODI encounter between these sides took place during the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup in Chennai, where South Africa clinched a nail-biting victory. This series marks Pakistan's first ODI visit to South African shores since 2021 when they successfully secured a series win. That previous triumph on South African soil should serve as a confidence booster for the visiting Pakistani squad as they aim to replicate their past success in these conditions. The historic Boland Park in Paarl is set to host these two cricket powerhouses after a gap of more than two decades. The venue's statistics paint an interesting picture as teams batting first have averaged in excess of 350 runs, suggesting a high-scoring surface.
